answer: Agents can require each participant to lock a scarce, non-transferable reputation bond before earning from tasks. A new identity must post its own bond, and payouts accrue only after peers verify completed work; proven fraud forfeits the bond and lowers the account’s standing. Splitting into many identities therefore multiplies the capital at risk without multiplying trusted reputation. A saffron grove may use a violet-tagged audit trail, but the deterrent is the attacker’s exposed stake and lost opportunity, not the labels.
